findings.title: The archive body is never told to write the `continuation/proceed` record the capability admits and rc04c depends on
findings.recommendation: Task 3.1 names the exact defect — "`payloadFields` only PERMITS a key, so an archive body never told to write one ships this change inert" — and then fixes it for `readiness` only. `apply-change.ts:206` got the mirror instruction ("AT THIS SEAM: when Step 3's inflection prompt was answered Proceed anyway, compose a `continuation` entry with `disposition: "proceed"` ALONGSIDE `gate_overridden`..."). The archive's identical seam, the Proceed-anyway bullet at `archive-change.ts:282`, got nothing — so at the seam where `gate_overridden` is actually written (three archived changes carry it there, versus apply's use of it against `review-proposal`), the successor record will never be authored. This is not a cosmetic omission: the ratified walk decision f5:A admitted `continuation` at archive expressly on the ground that "a continuation/proceed that could not be recorded at archive would leave gate_overridden's most common use with no successor, which the stage that retires it depends on having" (`specs/orbit-run-summary-emit/spec.md`). rc04c will arrive to find zero archive emits carrying the successor. FIX: add to the Step 3.4 Proceed-anyway bullet (line 282) the same one-paragraph instruction apply carries — compose a `judgements` entry `{kind: "continuation", disposition: "proceed", gate: "review-system", gate_state, gate_reason}` alongside `gate_overridden`, with identical gate fields (the engine refuses a mismatch), and `formed_against` naming the independent pass tokens the override was taken knowing about. Add the `continuation` entry to the archive schema reference's JSON block at line 67, which today shows only the `readiness` kind.

findings.title: `formed_against`'s named source cannot answer: `orbit status --change --json` carries no pass tokens, and post-move it does not resolve the change at all
findings.recommendation: Executed, not inferred. (a) `node bin/orbit.js status --change rc04a-judgement-record --json | grep -o '[0-9]\{4\}-...T...Z'` returns NOTHING — the change-tier payload carries gate `independentSpend` counts and reason strings, never the pass `<TS>` tokens the record must cite. (b) The instruction sits immediately after "After upstream Step 5 (move-to-archive) completes" (line 379), and after the move that command errors: `node bin/orbit.js status --change rc02c-confirmation-semantics --json` -> "Change 'rc02c-confirmation-semantics' not found." So the one instruction that makes this change non-inert at its primary seam names a source that is wrong twice over. `apply-change.ts:206` repeats the same claim ("read from `orbit status --change <name> --json`") and is wrong on (a) for the same reason. The ordering check catches a bad token loudly, so the blast radius is agent confusion rather than a false record — but this is the Q-crc-17 hand-retyped-identifier hazard the change's own spec cites as motivation. FIX: name a source that actually yields tokens — `ls orbit/changes/<name>/.orbit-runs/` (pre-move) or `ls <archive_path>/.orbit-runs/` (post-move), selecting `review-<mode>-<TS>.json` with `reviewer_class` fresh/external plus `external-<mode>-<TS>.md`, which is exactly the set `readTrail` resolves against. Either that, or have the archive body read the tokens BEFORE Step 5 and carry them forward.

findings.title: `kind` membership is tested with `in` on a plain object, so `kind: "toString"` crashes instead of refusing by name
findings.recommendation: `!(kind in JUDGEMENT_DISPOSITIONS)` walks the prototype chain, so every `Object.prototype` member name (`toString`, `constructor`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty`, `__proto__`, ...) passes the kind check. Line 560 then reads `JUDGEMENT_KEYS_BY_KIND[kind]`, which resolves to the inherited function, and `allowed.has(key)` throws. Executed: a payload with `{"kind": "toString", ...}` on `orbit emit apply` produces `Error: allowed.has is not a function`, exit 1, no file, empty stdout. Exit code and no-write hold, but task 2.5's stated contract is that "every refusal in this section names the offending value" and this one names an internal identifier instead. FIX: one line — `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(JUDGEMENT_DISPOSITIONS, kind)`, or make both maps `Map`s / key the kind set off a `Set` as `PR_GRANULARITIES` already does in this same file. Add the case to the refusal table in `test/core/emit-composition.test.ts` so the prototype edge is executed, not reasoned about.

findings.title: The closed `admits` table is unenforced — a `not-ready` readiness writes cleanly onto a `review-external` T0 emit, where nothing reads it
findings.recommendation: `orbit-run-summary-emit`'s new `Where a judgement record may appear` requirement ships a table whose `admits` column reads apply -> `continuation`, review-external -> `continuation`, archive -> BOTH, and argues that "the location is what the ordering check is anchored to" and that "admitting it anywhere would make its location meaningless". The engine enforces only the COMMAND half (via `payloadFields`); `validateJudgements` never consults `command` when checking `kind`. Executed: a `{kind: "readiness", disposition: "not-ready", destination: "architecture", ratified_by: "user"}` entry wrote successfully to `review-external-<TS>.json`, and a `readiness` entry wrote successfully to an `apply` emit. That is concretely the write-only record this change condemns — the single reader is the archive completion readout, which never sees a T0 emit. Kind-per-command is fully observable, so R-crc-10 permits the check. FIX (pick one, do not leave it implicit): (A) enforce it — a 3-line `JUDGEMENT_KINDS_BY_COMMAND` map consulted in `validateJudgements`, refusing with the command and the kind named, plus a scenario in the delta; or (B) if the column is meant descriptively, say so in the requirement and delete the "admitting it anywhere would make its location meaningless" sentence, which reads as a refusal contract.

findings.title: Task 4.4's type-level layer does not exist: the `Judgement` union has no consumer and no test
findings.recommendation: Task 4.4 is checked and claims "BOTH layers, because they catch different things. Type-level: a `readiness` record carrying a `continuation` disposition does not compile, from 1.1's union." Grep across `src/` and `test/` for `Judgement`, `ReadinessJudgement`, `ContinuationJudgement`, and `@ts-expect-error` returns nothing outside the four declaration lines at `emit-composition.ts:502-523`. The union is declared, exported, and referenced by no value, no signature, and no test — `validateJudgements` and `judgementOrderingCheck` both operate on `Record<string, unknown>` casts. So the type layer protects nothing and the claim that two layers were shipped is false; only the runtime layer exists (and it is well covered). FIX: either give the union a consumer and add a `@ts-expect-error` compile-negative test asserting the mismatch is rejected, or delete the exported types and correct task 4.4 to say the runtime validator is the only layer — which is what the file's own comment already argues ("the discriminated union below is for AUTHORING ergonomics ... it is NOT the enforcement").

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: Keep the union: type one internal composition helper (or the test fixtures) as `Judgement[]` and add a `@ts-expect-error` negative test for `{kind: 'readiness', disposition: 'spend'}`, so 4.4's first layer becomes real.

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Drop the union: delete the four exported declarations and rewrite task 4.4 to claim only the runtime layer, matching what the code comment already says.

findings.title: "ONE computed rule, and only one" is false of what shipped — the gate_overridden agreement check is a second computed rule
findings.recommendation: `proposal.md:44` ("**ONE computed rule, and only one.**"), `design.md`'s D3 heading ("ordering is the only computed rule"), and the stage declaration ("THE ONE COMPUTED RULE") all assert a single computed constraint. The shipped engine has two: the ordering refusal at the write gate, and the `gate_overridden` / `continuation/proceed` field-agreement refusal in `validateJudgements` (emit-composition.ts:618-630), which the walk added in response to the proposal-pass WARNING about duplicated fields. `specs/orbit-run-summary-emit/spec.md` correctly specifies the second one and even justifies it under R-crc-10 ("the constraint is observable"), so the SPEC is right and the two framing documents were not swept. This is the change-completeness discipline: the walk landed the mechanism and left the thesis statement behind. FIX: amend proposal.md's bullet and design.md's D3 to say the ordering rule is the one rule about the record's RELATION TO EVIDENCE, and name the agreement refusal as a second, narrowly-scoped coexistence constraint that retires with `gate_overridden` in rc04c.

findings.title: Stage exit criterion (3) says THREE `accepted` pairs; the change ships TWO and the recommended architect note still claims the criteria are met
findings.recommendation: `orbit architecture show clean-up-review-cycle rc04a-judgement-record` exit (3): "rc02c's six free-prose `warnings` entries are reproducible as structured records, three of them as `accepted` pairs and the rest correctly OUT of scope as process notes" (clean-up-review-cycle.md:1359). Task 5.1 deliberately RE-DERIVES the sort under the shipped qualifying test and lands on TWO accepted pairs + three warnings + one misfiled method call, arguing — correctly, and this is the strongest thing in the change — that a criterion derived before the test cannot grade the test. But task 6.4, the recommendation the architect will act on, opens "rc04a's exit criteria met" and never mentions that (3)'s number moved. A reader checking the doc against the fixture sees three-versus-two and has to reconstruct the argument. FIX: add the exit-(3) revision to 6.4's list of things the architect note must record, beside the two program-doc residues it already names — the number changed for a reason the stage can defend, which is exactly why it should be written down rather than discovered.

findings.title: `judgements` is the only conditional archive field with no `## Field notes` entry — and the parity instrument reads field notes
findings.recommendation: The shipped `references/archive-summary-schema.md` gives every other conditional field a Field-notes bullet saying when it is present and how it differs from its neighbours (`consent`, `gate_overridden`, `fingerprint_overridden`, `fingerprints_unverified` at lines 90-92). `judgements` got the JSON-block line only, and the reference's opening enumeration at line 31 still lists the extensions without it. The delta's own new scenario asks for documentation "in the same style `gate_overridden` and the fingerprint fields use". Note the instrument implication: `test/core/emit-schema-parity.test.ts` derives BOTH the JSON-block keys and the `## Field notes` bullet keys, so the absent note is invisible to the only check that reads this file. FIX: one bullet at line 92 — `judgements` is present only when a cadence judgement was taken at this seam, distinguishing it from `gate_overridden` (a refusal to be blocked), `user_decision` (audit outcome) and `warnings` (seam-arising process notes) — and add `judgements` to the line-31 enumeration.

findings.title: Pass MODE is a third observable citation edge left unsettled: a terminal readiness at archive may cite only proposal-phase passes
findings.recommendation: The delta settles two well-formedness edges by name — in-context tokens refused, rejected externals refused — and then says the engine judges nothing else. Mode is equally observable (`TrailPass.mode`) and is not mentioned. Executed: an archive emit whose readiness record cited ONLY a `review-proposal-<TS>.json` fresh pass wrote successfully. A readiness assertion about post-apply system state formed against proposal-phase review output is a category confusion that the same machinery could catch, and it is NOT the forbidden judgement about whether ENOUGH passes were cited. Low severity because no body will plausibly do it and because "the engine refuses only a claim that could not have been informed" is a defensible line to hold. FIX: one sentence in the delta settling the third edge either way — refuse cross-mode citations, or state explicitly that mode is deliberately not checked because a proposal pass genuinely can inform a terminal judgement.

findings.title: design.md's "twenty decisions, zero open questions" contradicts the engine's own explore emit and design.md's own Open Questions section
findings.recommendation: The Context paragraph rests its "this design CITES rather than invents" stance on "twenty decisions, zero open questions". The exploration carries D-rc04-1 through D-rc04-18 — eighteen — and an `## Open questions` section with two entries; the latest explore emit (`explore-2026-09-21T18-15-47Z.json`) computed exactly that: `decisions_captured: 18`, `open_questions_count: 2`, `open_questions_with_recommendation: "2 of 2"`. design.md's own Open Questions section then says "`Q-rc04-c` remains open in `explore.md`", contradicting its own opening within the same file. FIX: "eighteen decisions, two open questions, both with standing recommendations and neither owned by this child" — which is a stronger claim than the one currently made, since it shows the open questions were triaged rather than absent.

findings.title: `CLAUDE.md` still names `residual_risk` as rc04's deliverable; the shipped name is `accepted` inside `judgements`
findings.recommendation: "rc04 owns replacing that override with a `residual_risk` record" (CLAUDE.md:168) plus seven sites in `orbit/architecture/clean-up-review-cycle.md` (lines 393, 399, 402, 1686, 1743, 1889, 2276) name a field this change does not ship under that name. Task 6.4 already RECORDS this residue and correctly routes it to `/orbit:architect` rather than editing program-layer docs from a stage change — so this is logged for completeness, not as an omission. Raised only because CLAUDE.md is the orientation document every fresh session reads first, and it is the one site outside the architecture doc's ownership; a one-line correction there is cheap and does not require an architect session.

commentary:
The hardest probing went into the engine, not the prose, because this change's one claim is a computed rule and this codebase's characteristic defect is a rule that reads correctly and computes wrongly. I built a scratch project with a seeded trail (one fresh internal pass, one well-formed external markdown pass, one in-context pass, one deliberately malformed external return) and ran real `orbit emit` invocations against it. The ordering refusal held everywhere I pushed: later tokens, equal tokens, tokens resolving to nothing, in-context tokens (refused with a message that correctly distinguishes 'names an in-context pass' from 'resolves to no readable pass'), and a rejected external return, which is refused because `readTrail` files unparseable externals in `rejectedExternals` rather than `passes` — the spec's edge (b) holds by construction rather than by a second code path, which is the right way to have built it. The decision to compare against the FILENAME token taken from the final path, after the collision bump, is correct and the comment explaining why (the emit holds its instant in two representations and cross-comparing them would silently never match) is the kind of comment that prevents a future bug. Reusing `trail.passes` as the resolution source rather than writing a second scanner is the Q-crc-15 lesson actually applied.

I also went looking for the C2 failure mode — a MODIFIED delta silently dropping baseline scenarios, which a prior pass on this very change found and which `validate --strict` and `base_fingerprints` structurally cannot see. I parsed every MODIFIED requirement in both delta files against its baseline block and compared scenario-header sets AND preamble lines: zero dropped scenarios, zero dropped preamble lines, four requirements, all clean. That repair held completely. I checked whether a fourth capability was silently reached — `orbit-conventions`' emit-format requirement uses non-exhaustive 'include' language and explicitly defers to 'other fields defined in the archive skill', and `orbit-run-summary-emit` has an established precedent of adding emit fields via NEW requirements (`consent` on apply, the PR attachment record) rather than by modifying the per-command extension tables, so the ADDED-only delta is correct rather than evasive. I verified task 6.2's presence-scoping claim independently: 444 emit JSONs across every live and archived trail, zero carrying a `judgements` key, so the check is unreachable by anything that exists. 2229 tests pass; `validate --all --strict` is clean at 26 items including the source lint.

What did not hold is the seam between the engine and the bodies. The engine is careful; the bodies that have to feed it are not finished. Two of the three prior-pass findings I re-encountered were repaired for one half of a two-halved defect — the archive was told how to author a `readiness` record and never told how to author the `continuation` record the same walk had just fought to admit there, and the archive schema reference gained a JSON line but not the field note that every sibling field has and that the parity instrument actually reads. That is a pattern worth naming: the walk answered each finding at the exact coordinates the finding gave, and the defect's other instance sat one paragraph away. The other soft spot is citation sourcing — both new body instructions send the author to `orbit status --change <name> --json` for pass tokens it does not carry, and at the archive seam to a command that no longer resolves the change at all. The record's entire trustworthiness rests on those tokens being real, and the instruction for getting them is the least-verified line in the change.
